headline: Student Bakers Feed Hungry Children, One Cookie at a Time
meta_description: Frisco high school students turned their baking skills into a nonprofit raising over $8,000 for food-insecure children in their school district.
summary_short: Student-led nonprofit Baked Bites has raised $8,000 for hungry children by selling homemade cookies at pop-ups and through pre-orders across Frisco, Texas.
body:
A group of students in Frisco, Texas has built something quietly powerful: a student-led nonprofit called Baked Bites that has raised more than $8,000 for charitable causes by doing what they do best—baking cookies. Every dollar from pre-orders and community pop-ups goes directly to Frisco Fastpacs, a nonprofit partner that delivers weekend meal bags to more than 1,200 food-insecure children across Frisco ISD every Friday of the school year. For many of those children, these bags represent their primary food source when school is not in session. The founders grew up in the same school district they now serve, and they chose to transform a personal skill into community action, asking nothing but that all proceeds feed their neighbors.

What makes Baked Bites remarkable is its deliberate simplicity. There is no corporate backing or overhead extracting value from the mission—just students, homemade baked goods, and a community that keeps showing up to buy them. The founders are clear about what their $8,000 represents: not a fundraising milestone, but hundreds of people who chose to spend a few dollars on a cookie and, in doing so, chose to believe their neighbor's hunger was worth solving. A single weekend meal bag costs very little to fill, yet when enough small purchases accumulate, the math becomes undeniable: many children fed across many Saturdays.

This past summer marked Baked Bites' biggest season yet, with seven to eight bake sales, pop-ups, and community collaborations expanding their reach and bringing new supporters into the loop. Looking ahead, the group hopes to partner with local schools to connect students with resources and encouragement they might not otherwise encounter. It remains rooted in the same instinct that began it all: help the people around you with what you have, and keep going.
quick_facts: Partners with Frisco Fastpacs, serves 1,200+ kids
All proceeds from homemade cookies go to charity
Seven to eight pop-ups held during summer season
